A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same k-LPM research work. All 17 pages in each version, including equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C report original LLM-serving latency experiments, including TTFT curves and numerical results for varying prefix lengths.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C retain the original serving experiments and their reported latency measurements.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the oldest-query step followed by k−1 prefix-match steps. The correction to the analytical cost initialization in Definition 2 does not revise the scheduling procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same real-prompt serving workload and synthetic workloads with varying repeated-prefix lengths in Section 5 and Appendix C.

E2.justification: FCFS, LPM, and the same intermediate k-LPM configurations participate in the corresponding comparisons in both versions.

E3.justification: Both retain the same prompt counts, warm-up procedure, Poisson arrivals, model configurations, hardware, and TTFT metrics. Appendix C’s experimental settings also match.

E4.justification: The request-rate and k sensitivity analyses, additional latency-percentile plots, and Appendix C.2’s prefix-length-ratio analysis are unchanged.

E5.justification: Random-shuffling descriptions and statistical reporting remain unchanged. Neither version supplies empirical repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Figures 2–3 and Appendix C.2’s Table 1 contain identical results. No numerical entries, plotted trends, rankings, or reported empirical findings change.

T1.justification: Definition 2 changes R(j_1) = |x_{j_1}|^2 to R(j_1) = |x_{j_1}| + c_attn|x_{j_1}|^2, correcting the initial cost to incorporate the stated linear and attention terms. The remaining definitions, theorem statements, and proofs, including Appendices A–B, are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same claims concerning scheduling complexity, k-LPM’s theoretical and empirical advantages, and percentile-TTFT approximation.

C2.justification: The applicability discussion, cache and batching simplifications, interpretations of latency results, and limitations and future directions remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Reported SGLang implementation details, hardware, prompt construction, and benchmarking instructions are identical. Resource links are unchanged; only the PDF’s own arXiv version link is updated.

R1.justification: Section 1.2, the cited works, and the reference list are unchanged. The updated conference footer does not revise research positioning.

P1.justification: The first-page footer changes from 'Preprint. Under review.' to the NeurIPS 2025 conference notice, and the arXiv version/date are updated. Prose and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–3 and Table 1 retain identical formatting, captions, and placement. The equation and publication-text edits leave the page layout intact.

improvement.justification: The corrected initialization in Definition 2 better matches the stated processing-cost model, including the linear first-query cost when c_attn = 0 used in the analysis. This provides a limited improvement in mathematical consistency; empirical evidence and the remaining arguments are unchanged.
